items.title: 52150_Charlie Barnet oral history interview
items.q: And I worked for a whole year with Frank Weingard

ctx.x: Harry Voltaire (PHONETIC). There was nobody by the name of Brown in the whole band. It was just a bunch of guys that called themselves that. A fellow by the name of Harry Voltaire. And he gave me one lesson. I came back the next day and played him the whole score from "Wildflower", and instead of getting a pat on the head he read the riot act to me. Oh, he really laid me out for doing that. And I understand why now, because I was blessed with a good ear and he didn't want me to use the ear. He wanted me to learn…

people that. He'd say, "My, look at this kid here. He's got all the parts memorized." Well, this was fine, except we got -- we were going to make a record date, and we got in the studio there and we had this recording guy there by the name of Schubert (PHONETIC). I don't remember his first name, but he was one of those fellows that if you tapped an ashtray, he'd say, "That's a B." And we started, and he said, "Stop the band." He said, "Who is playing a G in the second and third beats of the fourth bar?" No…
